newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 20.78 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 20.78 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 88 basis points to 20.78 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 90 billion bolivars of 177- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 21.66 percent coupon for a price of 100.39 percent. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 21.66 percent

The bank also sold 30 billion bolivars of 268-day notes with a 22.24 percent coupon at a price of 99.64 percent, and 30 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 22.84 percent coupon at an average price of 98.60 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 89 basis points to 22.81 percent for the 268-day bills, but rose 55 basis points to 24.59 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
